transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-05
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya, Carlos, Priya, Leah, Dmitri, Ravi + whole company on listen-only

Summary (auto): Leadership overview and Q&A on priorities and risk posture.

00:00 Maya: All right welcome everybody, thanks for joining. we'll try to keep this tight to about an hour, we've got some slides in the deck and then open Q and A. Hi everybody.
00:14 Carlos: Quick housekeeping, slides are in the #all-hands channel, link in the chat, and we'll post recording after.
00:29 Maya: OK, state of the business, short version: ARR growth is healthy, usage volume up 2.3x year-over-year on hosted, Dedicated demand is picking up, we have three mid-enterprise deals in negotiation, runway unchanged after headcount pacing.
00:52 Priya: On the infra side we've been focused on reducing p99 generator latency, small wins this week with batching and kernel selection but some customers still see regressions at long sequences, so we have a targeted bugfix for next sprint.
01:12 Maya: Hiring thermostat — we continue to hire but more deliberately. we'll prioritize customer-facing SRE, a couple of infra engineers for GPU performance, and two sales engineers. Hiring freeze on non-critical ICs until the end of the quarter.
01:33 Leah: From CS, churn risk cluster is mostly SMBs who hit scaling surprises — we have a playbook being rolled out next week and more granular token-level billing example templates for customers.
01:51 Dmitri: Quick note on private deployments — the on-prem install kit has improved but we've seen tricky networking setups, VPC peering oddities. recommend a standard preflight checklist be mandated for all pilots.
02:09 Ravi: On encryption and KMS we validated HSM integration in the staging env, there was one key rotation bug, that's in the hotfix branch.
02:23 Maya: On product prioritization, high level: 1) reliability and SLOs, 2) Dedicated capacity GA polish, 3) Private deployment simplifications, 4) Optimize cost tooling — those are the trimmed priorities.
02:41 Carlos: For Dedicated GA — timeline is still end of Q1 but we need three things: SLA language, autoscale policy maturity, and smoke test suite for multi-tenant failures. Priya, Ravi can you confirm the checklist?
03:01 Priya: Yes, we have a draft checklist; I will attach it to the PR and add estimated effort per item. Some of the kernel-level perf as Dmitri mentioned needs more validation.
03:20 Maya: Want to call out SOC2 — compliance is on track, the security team closed 7 controls this sprint, but audit readiness needs artifact curation. Leah, work with security to prioritize customer-facing docs.
03:38 Leah: will do, starting with an FAQ for enterprise buyers and a short SOC2 snapshot for Sales.
03:49 (Audience chat: "Can we get more detail on pricing?" upvotes in the room)
04:02 Maya: pricing Q — we know customers ask about latency vs cost tradeoffs. we will publish an annotated pricing example that shows dedicated vs hosted economics by workload. Carlos will own that.
04:20 Carlos: I'll put together an annotated spreadsheet and examples with token-level breakdowns and quantization scenarios.
04:31 (brief pause, someone coughs)
04:35 Employee A (unsolicited): has anyone seen the KV cash issue on 2.4? it's spiking memory on long seqs.
04:47 Priya: probably mis-transcribed, KV cache, yes, we're on it, Ravi and I will pair on repro and a prioritized test.
05:02 Maya: ok moving to metrics — high-level ops thermometer: latency p50 ~ 110ms, p95 ~ 680ms, p99 ~ 1.8s on hosted for typical 1k token bursts, Dedicated numbers show better p95 but we still need variance reduction.
05:23 Dmitri: variance is driven by long-tail from cold KV cache and kernel fallback, we've prototyped more aggressive prefix caching to reduce that tail. initial numbers look promising but not baked.
05:43 Maya: a note on regressions and quality monitoring — we observed a generation regression on one of our largest customers after a model swap; that's the impetus for improved canary tooling and automated evals.
06:02 Carlos: we want per-route evals wired into rollouts, so a canary roll that fails quality threshold auto-rolls-back. roadmap item for Optimize.
06:17 Leah: On escalations — top three are (1) latency + billing confusion, (2) VPC onboarding friction, (3) SOC2 evidence requests. We'll publish playbooks for each.
06:34 (Audience question via Q&A box): "When will Dedicated be available in ap-southeast?"
06:41 Maya: Good question. We'll be region-ready after a limited beta; target is mid-Q2 for APAC in partnership with the cloud infra team.
06:52 Employee B: Can we get more transparency on sales commission linked to Dedicated GA?
07:01 Maya: sales comp details will be handled privately with Sales leadership; public note that bookings tied to Dedicated pilots will have MBOs.
07:15 (Slide flip sound)
07:18 Carlos: Product risks: we flagged two medium risks — model compatibility drift with quantized variants and customer network variability in private installs. Mitigations include expanded test matrix and network preflight checks.
07:39 Priya: technical deep-dive offer — we'll run two open office hours next week focusing on batching and kernel selection for app teams. RSVP on calendar.
07:50 (someone types in chat: "when's the next tech deep dive? pls")
07:56 Priya: calendar invite will go out today.
08:05 Maya: Now let's open to questions — we'll take a handful live and try to capture everything in the doc.
08:12 Q1 - Speaker 1: A question on the SOC2 timeline — how much of the external audit is in scope and when will we share artifacts?
08:25 Leah: We're completing pre-audit this sprint, external audit scheduled for late Q2. We'll share a sanitized artifact pack for sales enablement next week.
08:41 Q2 - Speaker 2: Regarding cost optimizations, can you share typical gains customers see from caching and quantization?
08:52 Carlos: typical ranges: caching can drop token compute by 20-40% on prefix-heavy workloads; quantization 8-bit can reduce GPU memory and cost materially but may need evals for quality; numbers vary widely by model and prompt.
09:14 Q3 - Speaker 3: Any updates on private air-gapped on-prem packaging?
09:22 Dmitri: Yes, the air-gapped bundle is delayed by a few weeks due to packaging and KMS integration; new estimate is early Q2. We want to make sure the install is repeatable and secure.
09:39 Q4 - Speaker 4: Can we get a short explainer on fallback policies and graceful degradation?
09:47 Maya: Sure — fallback policy is route-configurable, you can set region fallback, lower-capability model fallback, or queued burst policy. we'll publish examples.
10:03 (group laughter, someone mutes/unmutes)
10:11 Employee C: about the generation regression, is this rolling back models automatically?
10:18 Carlos: currently it's manual, we want to automate rollback once per-route evals find a drop below threshold, see roadmap.
10:31 (longer discussion between Priya and Ravi about repro steps; partial transcription)
10:31 Priya: so repro needs the long-seq manifest and a stable seed; Ravi can you share the perf harness?
10:41 Ravi: yes I'll upload the harness and a sample manifest to the infra repo later today.
10:53 Maya: Good. Action owners captured. We'll wrap with a quick recap.
11:03 Maya: Recap: trimmed priorities to reliability, Dedicated GA, Private simplification, Optimize cost tooling. Hiring thermostat tightened, action items assigned (see notes). We'll publish recordings and the trimmed deck tomorrow.
11:19 Leah: Thanks everyone, CS will send the escalation list and the SOC2 FAQ by Tuesday.
11:28 Maya: Thanks all, if you have more questions drop into the #all-hands or DM leadership. Meeting adjourned.

Auto sections (maybe incomplete):
Questions captured in chat: pricing examples, Dedicated GA in APAC, SOC2 artifacts, KV cache perf, private install timeline.
Action items repeated: see metadata.

Note on transcript quality: several technical segments had abbreviated names and a few mis-transcriptions (KV cache transcribed as K-V cash, Dedicated misspelled in a couple lines).
